centre.intro: Short answers to the questions people ask most. Can't find yours? Email us and a person will reply.

sizeGuide.title: Find your frame size
sizeGuide.intro: The easiest way is to copy a pair that already fits. Three numbers printed on its arm tell you almost everything.
sizeGuide.numbersTitle: Read the numbers on your glasses
sizeGuide.numbersBody: Look on the inside of an arm (sometimes the bridge). You'll see something like 52□18 140. All three are in millimetres.
sizeGuide.armLabel: Inside of a temple arm printed with 52, a small square, 18 and 140.

lens.name: 52: lens width
lens.body: The width of one lens. Most adult frames are 46 to 58 mm.

bridge.name: 18: bridge
bridge.body: The gap between the lenses, over your nose. A narrower bridge sits higher.

temple.name: 140: temple
temple.body: The arm's length, hinge to tip. 135 to 150 mm suits most adults.

sizeGuide.sizesBody: We group frames by their total front width. Within 2 to 3 mm of a pair you like will feel very similar.

noGlassesSteps.one: Stand in front of a mirror with a ruler or tape measure.
noGlassesSteps.two: Measure straight across your face from temple to temple, just beside your eyes.
noGlassesSteps.three: Choose frames whose width is within a few millimetres of that number. Each product page shows its width and a to-scale drawing.

comfortTips.bridge: If glasses slide down your nose, try a narrower bridge or frames with adjustable nose pads.
comfortTips.temples: Arms that press behind your ears are too short; ones that stick out past them are too long.
comfortTips.pads: Metal and titanium frames have adjustable pads, which any optician can fine-tune in a minute.

prescription.title: How to read your prescription
prescription.intro: A prescription looks cryptic, but it's only a few numbers per eye. Here's what each one means.
prescription.exampleCaption: Example prescription with sphere, cylinder, axis and addition for each eye
prescription.exampleNote: Minus numbers correct short sight (distance is blurry); plus numbers correct long sight. Your prescription may leave some boxes empty.

sph.name: SPH (sphere)
sph.body: The main power of the lens, in dioptres. Minus for short sight, plus for long sight.

cyl.name: CYL (cylinder)
cyl.body: Extra power for astigmatism, when the eye focuses differently in one direction. Empty means none.

axis.name: AXIS
axis.body: The direction of the cylinder, from 1 to 180 degrees. It only appears with a CYL value.

add.name: ADD (addition)
add.body: Extra magnification for reading, used for progressive and reading lenses. It is usually the same for both eyes.

pd.name: PD (pupillary distance)
pd.body: The distance between the centres of your pupils, so the optical centre of each lens sits in front of each eye.

prescription.validityBody: Eye-care professionals generally recommend an eye test every one to two years. If your vision has changed since your last test, get a new prescription before ordering.

returns.title: Returns and warranty
returns.intro: Not right? Return any order within {days} days of delivery for a full refund, prescription lenses included.

steps.one: Within {days} days of delivery, email {email} with your order number and what you'd like to return.
steps.two: We reply within one working day with a free pickup slot.
steps.three: Pack the glasses in their case and box. Our courier collects them from your address.
steps.four: We check them when they arrive and refund you straight away.

returns.refundsBody: Refunds go back to the way you paid, within 5 to 7 working days of the return reaching us. Cash-on-delivery orders are refunded to a UPI ID or bank account you give us.
returns.warrantyBody: Every frame is covered for {months} months from delivery against manufacturing faults. We repair or replace it free, including shipping.

warrantyList.covered: Covered: loose or broken hinges, peeling coatings, cracks that appear without an impact.
warrantyList.notCovered: Not covered: accidental damage, scratches from wear, or loss.

rx.sphHelp: The main power. Minus for short sight (distance is blurry), plus for long sight. 0.00 or 'plano' means no correction.
rx.cylHelp: Corrects astigmatism. Leave it empty if your prescription has no cylinder.
rx.axisHelp: The angle of the cylinder, from 1 to 180. It is only used with a cylinder.
rx.addHelp: The extra power for reading, used by progressive lenses. It is usually the same for both eyes.
rx.pdHelp: The distance between your pupils in millimetres, so the centre of each lens sits in front of your eye. Two numbers mean each eye is measured from the middle of your nose.
rx.measureStep1: Stand about 20 cm from a mirror and hold a millimetre ruler flat against your brow.
rx.measureStep2: Close your right eye and line up 0 with the centre of your left pupil.
rx.measureStep3: Open your right eye, close your left, and read the number at the centre of your right pupil. Most adults measure between 54 and 74 mm.
